questions.question: What is the purpose of a circuit breaker?
questions.tutor: Circuit breaker automatically interrupts fault current to protect equipment.

questions.question: What is the difference between a fuse and a circuit breaker?
choices: Fuse is one-time; breaker can be reset
Breaker is one-time; fuse can be reset
questions.tutor: Fuse melts once and must be replaced; breaker trips and can be reset.

questions.question: What does a ground fault circuit interrupter (GFCI) protect against?
questions.tutor: GFCI detects imbalance between hot and neutral (leakage to ground).

questions.question: What is the typical trip sensitivity of a GFCI?
questions.tutor: GFCI trips at 4-6 mA to protect against electric shock.

questions.question: What does an AFCI protect against?
questions.tutor: AFCI detects dangerous arcing that could cause fire.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a lightning arrester?
questions.tutor: Lightning arrester clamps overvoltage and diverts surge current to ground.

questions.question: What is a relay in power systems?
questions.tutor: Protective relay senses fault and sends signal to circuit breaker.

questions.question: What is an overcurrent relay?
questions.tutor: Overcurrent relay operates when current exceeds predetermined value.

questions.question: What is ANSI device number 50?
questions.tutor: ANSI 50 = Instantaneous overcurrent relay.

questions.question: What is ANSI device number 51?
questions.tutor: ANSI 51 = Time overcurrent relay (inverse time).

questions.question: What is ANSI device number 87?
questions.tutor: ANSI 87 = Differential protection relay.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a differential relay?
questions.tutor: Differential relay trips if difference between input and output currents exceeds threshold.

questions.question: What is a recloser?
choices: Automatically restores power after temporary fault
questions.tutor: Recloser opens on fault and recloses; clears temporary faults.

questions.question: What is a sectionalizer?
choices: Isolates faulted section after recloser opens
questions.tutor: Sectionalizer opens after counting fault current interruptions.

questions.question: What is the interrupting rating of a circuit breaker?
choices: Maximum fault current it can interrupt
questions.tutor: Interrupting rating is the maximum fault current breaker can safely clear.

questions.question: What is the difference between fuse and circuit breaker time-current curve?
choices: Fuse has inverse time; breaker can be adjusted
questions.tutor: Both have inverse time characteristics, but breakers often have adjustable trip settings.

questions.question: What is a ground fault relay?
questions.tutor: Ground fault relay measures residual or zero-sequence current.

questions.question: What is the typical time delay for a fuse to blow at 10x rated current?
questions.tutor: At high overcurrent, fuse blows very fast (milliseconds to 0.1 sec).

questions.question: What is a motor protection relay?
choices: Protects against overload, stall, phase loss
questions.tutor: Motor protection includes overload, locked rotor, phase unbalance, and ground fault.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a thermal overload relay?
questions.tutor: Thermal overload relay mimics motor heating curve to protect from overheating.

questions.question: What is a magnetic circuit breaker?
questions.tutor: Magnetic breaker uses solenoid to trip instantly on short circuit.

questions.question: What is a thermal-magnetic circuit breaker?
choices: Combination of thermal overload and magnetic short circuit protection
questions.tutor: Thermal element for overload (slow), magnetic for short circuit (instant).

questions.question: What is the purpose of a surge protective device (SPD)?
questions.tutor: SPD clamps voltage spikes from lightning or switching.

questions.question: What is the typical response time of a surge arrester?
questions.tutor: Surge arresters respond in nanoseconds to divert fast-rising surges.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a current limiting fuse?
choices: Limits peak fault current before it reaches zero
questions.tutor: Current-limiting fuse melts and creates high resistance before first current peak.
